solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flinch from bells in church

indicators.note: in places the bells word inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to ring is what bells do; ring is also a set of bells

explanation.surface: Someone recoils at the din of church bells.
explanation.definitionFit: To flinch is to shrink back or wince in fear or embarrassment, a close synonym.

clue.text: Bind helium in nucleus

indicators.note: in puts the helium symbol within the word for nucleus

parts.note: the core of something is its nucleus
He is the chemical symbol for helium

explanation.surface: A physics note: helium sits bound in an atomic nucleus.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that bind together stick or hold together, which is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Aggrieved nitrogen is put in cocktail of gin and it

indicators.note: is put in places the nitrogen symbol inside the mixed letters
a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of these words are mixed up

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Someone is upset that nitrogen has been added to their gin-and-it, a gin and vermouth drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail of' scrambles GIN AND IT into INDIGANT, and 'is put in' places N inside it. Gin and it is a real cocktail, which hides the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggrieved means resentful at unfair treatment, the same feeling as righteous anger.

clue.text: Noble is good currency

parts.note: the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: A nobleman claims to be good money.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble in the sense of magnificent, stately or dignified; a synonym.

clue.text: Great loss of liquid for flushing toilet

parts.note: water is the commonest liquid
loo is British slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A plumbing complaint: a toilet wastes great quantities of liquid when flushed.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo, Napoleon's 1815 defeat, is used for any crushing defeat. 'Great loss' looks like a leak.
explanation.definitionFit: Meeting one's Waterloo means suffering a decisive defeat, after Napoleon's final battle.

clue.text: Like St Augustine, reformed as a Hippo cleric

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: St Augustine, Bishop of Hippo, cast as a cleric who reformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' rearranges AS A HIPPO CLERIC. St Augustine of Canterbury was the first Archbishop of Canterbury, while Augustine of Hippo, the clue's nod, was only a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to an archbishop, and St Augustine of Canterbury was the first holder of that see.

clue.text: Treasury reported former auditor

indicators.note: reported signals that the words heard spoken give the answer

parts.note: an ex (former) checker (auditor), one who once checked accounts

explanation.surface: A former auditor was reported to the Treasury.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exchequer is the British government department managing public revenue, the Treasury.

clue.text: Left meal unstarted? Far from the greatest

indicators.note: unstarted means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a feast is a large meal

explanation.surface: Someone left their meal untouched, hardly the best effort.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of little is the very opposite of the greatest, the smallest amount.

clue.text: Too much work? Right for a ruler

indicators.note: Right for a means the right letter takes the place of the letter a

parts.note: an overload is too much work

explanation.surface: Is a boss right to set too much work?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right for a' swaps the A of OVERLOAD for R.
explanation.definitionFit: An overlord is a supreme ruler or lord over other lords.

clue.text: Worldwide movement ruins it with stale concept

indicators.note: ruins means wrecks, so these letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A global campaign spoiled by a tired idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruins' shuffles IT and STALE CONCEPT; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The theory of crustal plates describes how the Earth's surface shifts across the whole globe.

clue.text: Chair duly suffers damage linked to pressure and movement

indicators.note: suffers damage means the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: An office chair is broken by pressure and movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydraulic systems use fluid pressure to drive motion, as in a hydraulic chair lift.

clue.text: Aspire to constant rapturous reception

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, notably the speed of light
a rave is a rapturous review or welcome

explanation.surface: A performer longs for constant applause.
explanation.definitionFit: To crave something is to long for it eagerly, just as one aspires to a goal.

clue.text: Cocaine, perhaps unopened in a wrap

indicators.note: unopened means the first letter is removed

parts.note: cocaine is an example of a drug

explanation.surface: Cocaine sold in a wrap, the folded paper dealers use.
explanation.definitionFit: A rug is a blanket or travelling rug used to wrap someone up.

clue.text: Causing harm for the teeth eating alien marge

indicators.note: eating means the outer word swallows the others

parts.note: dental means relating to teeth
ET is the film alien
marge is short for margin, here a rim

explanation.surface: Margarine is bad for the teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marge' is not margarine but short for margin, so RIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Something detrimental does damage, which is the same as causing harm.

clue.text: Rodent damage returning to motorway

parts.note: to mar is to damage
M is used for motorway, as in M1

indicators.note: returning means the word to is read backwards

explanation.surface: A rodent causes damage on the way back to the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: The marmot is a large burrowing ground squirrel, a kind of rodent.

clue.text: Second number scheme on European aircraft

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: A further numbered plan for a European aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-winged aeroplane, a type of aircraft.

clue.text: Piano and old furniture fitter

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, softly
lumber is old unwanted furniture

explanation.surface: Someone fits a piano and old furniture into a room.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who fits pipes and water systems, so a type of fitter.

clue.text: Engineered wrong bits for missile launcher

indicators.note: engineered means constructed anew, so the letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Faulty parts were built into a rocket launcher.
explanation.definitionFit: The cord of a bow launches its missile, the arrow.

clue.text: Plant cannabis in container in the kitchen

parts.note: stock is a garden flower
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone grows cannabis in a pot in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A large pot for making stock or soup, a piece of kitchenware.

clue.text: Very large birds get caught

parts.note: tit and ani are both birds, the ani a kind of cuckoo
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Huge birds being captured.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means gigantic, like the Titans of myth.

clue.text: Eccentric boasted when cutting southern Yankee

indicators.note: cutting means splitting the others, so the boasted word goes between them

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO alphabet
crew is an old past tense of crow, to boast

explanation.surface: An odd person bragged about wounding a man from the South.
explanation.walkthrough: CREW, the old past tense of crow, sits between S and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwy is informal for crazy or odd, as is eccentric.

clue.text: Tangle with philosopher over life being empty

parts.note: Carl Jung, the Swiss psychiatrist and thinker

indicators.note: being empty means the inside letters are removed, leaving the outside ones

explanation.surface: A wrangle with a philosopher about a meaningless life.
explanation.definitionFit: A jungle is a confused tangle, of vegetation or anything else.

clue.text: Harsh policeman with reduced integrity in short case

indicators.note: in places the policeman and integrity inside the case
short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a case, as a container
cop is slang for a policeman

indicators.note: reduced means a letter is cut off the end

parts.note: honour means integrity

explanation.surface: A corrupt policeman in a minor court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a court case but is a container. 'short' and 'reduced' each drop a final letter, and 'in' encloses the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacophonous describes a harsh, discordant sound.

clue.text: Approximately round figure down by a third on area

indicators.note: down by a third means a third of the word's six letters are cut from the end

parts.note: a circle is a round figure

explanation.surface: A statistician estimates a figure rounded down by a third.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round figure' suggests rounding a number; it is a geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Circa, Latin for around, means roughly, used with dates.

clue.text: Capture a number of French

definitions.meaning: to take hold of or grab

explanation.surface: Capturing several Frenchmen.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize is to capture; seize is also French for sixteen.

clue.text: Mostly stressed foreign consonant

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taut means stressed or tense

explanation.surface: A foreign consonant that mostly carries emphasis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stressed' looks like linguistic emphasis but means tense.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek letter, sounding T, so a consonant from a foreign alphabet.

clue.text: Jacket father used to cover chest

indicators.note: used to cover means the father word goes round the other

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
an ark is a chest, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: Dad used a jacket to cover his chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof jacket.

clue.text: Just thinking I am against being involved with golf

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
agin is dialect for against
in means involved with
G is golf in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfer protests they are only musing about opposing the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagining something is merely picturing it in the mind, not doing it.

clue.text: Disinclined on time runs to ski diagonally

indicators.note: on here means the disinclined word comes after, placed on the time and runs letters

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
averse means disinclined

explanation.surface: A reluctant skier, short of time, crosses the runs at an angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts AVERSE after T and R. 'runs' suggests ski runs but is the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: In skiing, a traverse is crossing a slope at an angle rather than straight down.

clue.text: Fish of poor quality

definitions.meaning: a Mediterranean food fish of the drum family

explanation.surface: A fish of poor quality.
explanation.definitionFit: The meagre is a large edible sea fish; meagre also means scanty.
